description:
Six aspiring engineers, six different backgrounds, and somehow, one team.
We came together through curiosity and a willingness to try something new. With skills in coding, research, design, and problem-solving, we turn different perspectives into creative solutions. We're curious and adaptable. We may not have all the answers, but we'll figure it out together.
summary:
Don't you ever feel like Earth is getting crowded?
Isn't it time to make Mars our next home?

MAVEN 2 begins with the lessons of a fictional failed mission, MAVEN 1, and asks one important question: Can we do better?

LEVEL 1 | Build. Drive. Explore.
Design a 3D Mars rover, choose its components, and explore Martian terrain through missions at different difficulty levels. Build your own rover or choose a ready-made one.

LEVEL 2 | Plan. Launch. Survive.
Prepare a crewed Mars mission by selecting instruments and supplies, balancing payload limits, and managing resources throughout the 180-day journey to Mars.

LEVEL 3 | Discover. Learn. Continue.
Explore Mars through six scientific missions, guided by a character inspired by Viking 2, who shares the mission's story before helping you investigate habitats, oxygen production, water, radiation, and plant growth.

MAVEN 2 turns space exploration into an interactive learning experience that builds engineering, planning, and problem-solving skills.

Because a failed mission isn't the end. It's the beginning of a better one.
details:
MAVEN 2

One Game. Three NASA Challenges. One Journey.

Learn from failure. Survive the mission. Build the future.

1. What Does MAVEN 2 Do?

MAVEN 2 is an interactive educational Mars exploration game that transforms complex space exploration concepts into a connected, story-driven experience.

The game follows one ambitious question:

Can humans prepare for a sustainable future on Mars?

The story begins with a fictional mission created specifically for the game, MAVEN 1, which failed to achieve its primary objectives. Its failure provides valuable lessons that shape the development of MAVEN 2.

The player enters the mission as an astronaut candidate, completes training, joins a six-member crew, and eventually becomes Co-Commander. Guided by Mission Commander Rodaina and the rest of the crew, the player progresses through three connected levels that form one continuous journey.

Throughout this journey, MAVEN 2 brings together three NASA Space Apps Challenge themes through interconnected gameplay, combining rover engineering, human space mission planning, and the history and science of Mars exploration.

LEVEL 1 — Build. Drive. Explore.

The journey begins with rover engineering.

Players design their own 3D Mars rover by selecting components and observing how each decision affects the rover's mass, power consumption, configuration, and capabilities.

They then move from designing to operating: navigating Martian terrain, avoiding obstacles, managing battery power, and completing exploration missions.

Your Rover. Your Decisions. Your Mission.

One of the most important features of this level is that the rover players design is not just a model to look at — it is the actual rover they will use during the missions.

Players have two options:

  • Build their own rover by selecting its components.
  • Choose a ready-made rover provided by the game and start exploring.

The design choices directly affect gameplay. Different components unlock or restrict certain commands, meaning that the rover's configuration determines which actions are available to the player. Players must therefore consider their design choices before starting a mission.

The game offers three difficulty levels, and the maps within each difficulty level can change, giving players different exploration conditions and challenges rather than repeating exactly the same experience.

An Autopilot option is also available to assist players with navigation. However, it is not designed to handle everything independently. It provides assistance while leaving room for the player to take manual control, make decisions, and actively operate the rover.

This creates a balance between automation and hands-on learning: players can benefit from assistance without losing the experience of controlling their own rover.

Players learn that a successful rover is not necessarily the most powerful one; it is the one designed for its mission.

LEVEL 2 — Plan. Launch. Survive.

After completing the rover exploration stage, players move on to a more advanced challenge: preparing for and managing a long-duration human mission to Mars.

The player joins a six-person crew and begins preparing the spacecraft for the journey.

Before launch, players select scientific instruments, equipment, and essential supplies while considering important payload constraints, including total mass, available volume, power requirements, and crew needs.

Understand Your Equipment. Prepare Your Mission. Explore the Journey.

When players select a piece of equipment or a scientific instrument, they can click on it to view an explanation of its purpose and function. This helps them understand what they are choosing and why it matters to the mission, rather than selecting equipment without knowing its role.

The preparation process also includes an option to automatically transfer selected equipment and supplies to the spacecraft, reducing unnecessary back-and-forth actions and making the planning experience smoother.

During the journey, players can interact with a 3D visualization of the spacecraft, follow its progress, move around it, and view it from different angles. This makes the journey more immersive and gives players a better visual understanding of the spacecraft.

The mission includes a 180-day outbound journey to Mars and a 180-day return journey. Throughout this long-duration mission, players must monitor the spacecraft's systems, manage available resources, and respond to unexpected situations.

Possible mission events include:

  • Water Recovery Decline: The water recovery system becomes less efficient, reducing the available water supply.
  • Insufficient Electrical Energy: Power generation or availability becomes insufficient to support all spacecraft systems.
  • Oxygen Generation Failure: The oxygen generation system stops functioning properly, threatening the crew's life-support conditions.
  • Radiation Alert: The crew receives a radiation warning and must respond to the potential exposure risk.
  • Crew Fatigue: Crew members experience fatigue, affecting their ability to perform mission tasks.
  • Communication Interruption: Contact with mission control is temporarily disrupted.
  • Equipment Malfunction: A critical piece of equipment develops a fault and requires attention.

Players must continuously monitor and manage essential mission resources, including:

  • Food
  • Water
  • Oxygen
  • Electrical Power
  • Supplies
  • Crew Health

Every decision involves trade-offs. Choosing additional equipment may improve mission capabilities but increase payload mass or power consumption. Using resources for one system may limit what remains available for another.

MAVEN 2 focuses on several key aspects of space mission design, including mission preparation, scientific instrument selection, payload constraints, resource allocation, spacecraft operations, and responses to unexpected events. These elements allow players to experience important engineering and operational trade-offs during a long-duration Mars mission.

What the Player Learns:

A successful space mission depends on careful planning, understanding equipment, resource management, teamwork, and the ability to respond to unexpected problems.

LEVEL 3 — Discover. Learn. Continue.

After completing the journey to Mars, players begin exploring the Martian surface and investigating the possibilities and challenges of future human exploration.

During the landing sequence, as the spacecraft settles on the Martian surface, players can see Viking 1, with its name visibly displayed on the lander. This visual encounter introduces a historical reference to NASA's early Mars exploration missions.

Later in the game, players meet a personified representation of the Viking 2 mission. This character first introduces himself by sharing the story, background, and scientific contributions of the original mission. After this introduction, he becomes the players' guide, helping them understand their objectives, organize their tasks, and navigate the challenges of exploring the Martian environment.

Learn from Previous Missions. Make Better Decisions.

With Viking 2's guidance, players complete six scientific and exploration missions:

  1. Select a Safe Habitat Site: Evaluate terrain stability, surface slope, and environmental conditions to identify a suitable location for a future habitat.
  2. Map the Surface and Plan Expansion: Explore the surrounding area, identify obstacles, map possible routes, and plan suitable zones for future infrastructure.
  3. Produce Oxygen: Investigate how oxygen can be produced using resources available in the Martian atmosphere.
  4. Find and Evaluate Water: Search for potential water-ice resources and assess their accessibility and usability for future missions.
  5. Radiation Mapping and Protection: Investigate radiation levels and understand the importance of protecting astronauts and habitats from radiation exposure.
  6. Regolith and Controlled Growing: Explore Martian soil properties and investigate the possibilities of growing plants under controlled conditions.

After completing the missions, players receive a mission report summarizing their progress, discoveries, and results.

Through this level, players connect the history of Mars exploration with scientific investigation and the challenges of preparing for future human missions.

2. What Benefits Does It Have?

MAVEN 2 turns space exploration from something students only read about into something they can actively experience.

It helps players:

  • Understand the engineering decisions behind rover design.
  • Explore the relationship between equipment, mass, energy, and performance.
  • Learn how component selection affects rover capabilities and available commands.
  • Understand why resource management is essential for long-duration space missions.
  • Discover the purpose of scientific instruments and mission equipment.
  • Understand the challenges of oxygen, water, food, power, radiation, and crew health.
  • Explore the importance of previous Mars missions in guiding future exploration.
  • Develop problem-solving, critical-thinking, planning, and decision-making skills.
  • Understand that failures are part of scientific progress and can provide valuable lessons for future missions.

The game is designed to make space science more accessible and engaging, particularly for students and young people interested in STEM.

3. What Is the Intended Impact?

Our goal is to make Mars exploration understandable and engaging for a wider audience.

Instead of presenting space exploration as a collection of scientific facts, MAVEN 2 connects those facts through an interactive journey in which players experience the decisions, challenges, and consequences involved in a Mars mission.

We aim to:

  • Encourage interest in space science, engineering, and technology.
  • Introduce younger audiences to real scientific and engineering concepts through gameplay.
  • Demonstrate the importance of teamwork and interdisciplinary thinking.
  • Promote scientific curiosity and learning through experimentation.
  • Help players understand the complexity of preparing for future human exploration of Mars.
  • Inspire players to think about sustainability, resource efficiency, and the challenges of living beyond Earth.

Ultimately, we want players to leave the game with a different perspective: reaching Mars is not just about getting there; it is about understanding the planet, managing its challenges, and preparing responsibly for what comes next.

4. What Tools and Technologies Did We Use?

MAVEN 2 is a browser-based project developed using web technologies.

Programming and Development

  • HTML: Structuring the game's pages and interfaces.
  • CSS: Designing layouts, visual elements, and interactive interfaces.
  • JavaScript: Implementing game logic, interactions, and simulation behavior.

Libraries and Technologies

  • Three.js: Creating and displaying the interactive 3D rover-design experience.
  • Canvas 2D: Supporting visual rendering and interactive elements.
  • Tailwind CSS: Supporting interface styling.
  • Local Storage: Saving player configurations and selected options locally.
  • JSON: Organizing equipment, spacecraft, and resource configuration data.

Creative and AI-Assisted Tools

  • Google Gemini
  • ChatGPT
  • Claude
  • Google Antigravity
  • Google Flow

These tools supported different parts of the creative and development process, including research, idea development, content organization, problem-solving, visual creation, and development assistance.

The project is software-based and does not require dedicated physical hardware.

5. How Is MAVEN 2 Creative?

The main creative idea behind MAVEN 2 is bringing three different NASA challenge themes together in one connected game instead of treating them as separate educational activities.

The game is structured around three stages of one larger mission:

  • Level 1: Build the technology needed to explore Mars.
  • Level 2: Prepare the crew and plan a mission that can survive the journey.
  • Level 3: Explore Mars, investigate its resources, and understand what future human presence would require.

The three levels are connected through one storyline, recurring characters, mission progression, and decisions that make the experience feel like one continuous journey. Each stage contributes to the overall response to the selected NASA challenge themes.

We also combine different ways of learning: 3D engineering, interactive rover exploration, mission planning, resource management, scientific investigation, and narrative storytelling.

Several gameplay features make this experience more than a traditional educational game:

  • The rover design directly affects the commands and actions available during gameplay.
  • Players can choose between building their own rover and using a ready-made one.
  • Autopilot assists the player without completely replacing manual control.
  • Changing maps and three difficulty levels provide different exploration experiences.
  • Equipment explanations help players understand the scientific purpose of their choices.
  • Automatic equipment transfer makes mission preparation more convenient.
  • Interactive spacecraft viewing allows players to explore the journey from different angles.
  • Viking 1 provides a visual historical reference during the landing sequence.
  • Viking 2 introduces himself to players before guiding them through the Mars exploration tasks.

Another important creative element is the role of failure. MAVEN 1 is not simply a background story; it establishes the reason behind MAVEN 2. The player is encouraged to learn from previous setbacks, make better decisions, and understand that progress in science and engineering often comes through testing, adaptation, and improvement.

6. What Factors Did Our Team Consider?

While developing MAVEN 2, we considered several important factors:

Scientific and Educational Accuracy

We aimed to base the game's concepts on real Mars exploration challenges and scientific principles. The game uses recognizable concepts such as rover engineering, resource management, oxygen production, water investigation, radiation protection, and controlled agriculture.

Technical Feasibility

We considered the limitations of developing an interactive game within the available time. We focused on creating a browser-based experience using accessible web technologies and dividing the project into manageable components.

Gameplay and User Experience

We designed the levels to progress from engineering activities to more complex mission decisions. The player should understand what to do, why each decision matters, and how actions affect mission outcomes.

We also considered accessibility and ease of interaction through equipment explanations, automatic transfer options, and assisted navigation.

Resource and System Constraints

We considered the relationships between mass, volume, energy, supplies, equipment performance, and crew requirements. These constraints help make the experience more connected to the realities of space mission planning.

Story and Continuity

We wanted the three NASA challenge themes to feel like parts of one mission, not unrelated mini-games. Characters, mission briefings, events, and progression connect the player's experience from astronaut training to Mars exploration.

The historical appearances of Viking 1 and Viking 2 also help connect previous Mars exploration efforts to the player's own journey.

Development and Future Improvement

We distinguished the developed MVP from the broader vision of the complete game. The current project brings the three levels into one experience, with rover design in Level 1, payload and instrument selection in Level 2, and the Mars exploration storyline and mission objectives in Level 3.

Some mechanisms, calculations, and system behaviors can still benefit from further testing, validation, and refinement.

7. NASA Challenge Objectives & How We Addressed Them

MAVEN 2 brings together three NASA Space Apps Challenge themes through one connected game. Rather than assigning one challenge to each level, the project combines related concepts across the three stages of the player's journey.

Challenge 1 — Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

How MAVEN 2 addresses it:

MAVEN 2 introduces players to important engineering and operational challenges involved in Mars exploration. Through rover design and operation, players explore how engineering choices affect mission capabilities. Across the connected levels, they also encounter resource-management and environmental challenges related to future human exploration.

The current experience focuses on rover engineering, exploration, and mission-related resource decisions, providing a foundation for expanding into more comprehensive outpost management.

  • Players design a 3D rover by selecting components.
  • They observe how component choices affect mass, power consumption, configuration, and capabilities.
  • The rover they design is used directly in gameplay.
  • Players can choose between building their own rover and selecting a ready-made one.
  • Different components unlock or restrict available commands.
  • Three difficulty levels and changing maps provide different exploration conditions.
  • Assisted Autopilot supports navigation while preserving player control.

What the player learns: How engineering choices influence a rover's ability to complete its mission, and how automation can support human operation without replacing it.

Challenge 2 — Space Mission Design Game

How MAVEN 2 addresses it:

MAVEN 2 focuses on several key aspects of space mission design, including mission preparation, scientific instrument selection, payload constraints, resource allocation, spacecraft operations, and responses to unexpected events. These elements allow players to experience important engineering and operational trade-offs during a long-duration Mars mission.

  • Built a mission preparation experience for a six-member crew.
  • Included scientific instrument and equipment selection.
  • Provided explanations of selected equipment and its purpose.
  • Considered payload mass, available volume, power, and supply requirements.
  • Included an option to automatically transfer selected equipment and supplies to the spacecraft.
  • Introduced food, water, oxygen, and other essential mission resources.
  • Developed a journey narrative involving a 180-day outbound trip and a 180-day return trip.
  • Included mission events that challenge players to respond to equipment failures, resource shortages, radiation alerts, and crew fatigue.
  • Allowed players to explore the spacecraft journey visually from different viewing angles.

What the player learns: A successful space mission depends on careful planning, understanding equipment, resource management, teamwork, and the ability to respond to unexpected problems.

Challenge 3 — Abandoned but Not Forgotten

How MAVEN 2 addresses it:

  • MAVEN 2 introduces the history of Mars exploration through references to NASA's Viking missions and connects their legacy to the scientific questions that future exploration must investigate.
  • During the landing sequence, players see the Viking 1 lander on the Martian surface, with its name visibly displayed.
  • Later, a personified representation of Viking 2 introduces the original mission's story and background before guiding players through their exploration tasks.
  • The game connects this historical introduction to six scientific missions covering:
    • Habitat-site evaluation.
    • Surface mapping.
    • Oxygen production.
    • Water investigation.
    • Radiation protection.
    • Controlled plant growing.
  • These elements provide a historical starting point for understanding previous Mars exploration efforts.
  • Future Development: Expand the experience to explore the functions, discoveries, and scientific contributions of abandoned Mars equipment.

What the player learns: Previous Mars missions provide valuable historical and scientific context that can help us understand the planet and prepare for future exploration.

8. NASA Judging Criteria — How MAVEN 2 Meets Them

1. Impact

What it evaluates: The potential value and reach of the project's impact.

How we address it:

MAVEN 2 aims to make space science and Mars exploration more accessible to students and young audiences. By turning complex concepts into interactive experiences, the game can encourage interest in STEM fields and help players understand real challenges in space exploration.

Its impact is not limited to entertainment: it aims to build curiosity, scientific awareness, and an understanding of engineering and mission planning.

2. Creativity

What it evaluates: The originality and innovation of the project's approach.

How we address it:

Our main creative approach is combining three NASA challenge themes into one connected game with a continuous storyline.

Rather than creating three independent activities, we designed a progression from rover engineering to crewed mission planning and then Mars surface investigation.

The fictional failure of MAVEN 1 also gives the game a meaningful narrative foundation: players do not simply complete tasks; they participate in a mission built around learning from previous mistakes.

The rover-to-gameplay connection, assisted Autopilot, interactive spacecraft viewing, and Viking 1 and Viking 2 appearances add further creative elements to the experience.

3. Validity

What it evaluates: Whether the solution is scientifically and technically grounded and whether it can do what it claims to do.

How we address it:

We based the game's educational concepts on recognizable scientific and engineering principles, including:

  • Rover mass, power, and component selection.
  • Spacecraft payload and resource limitations.
  • Food, water, and oxygen requirements.
  • Radiation exposure and protection.
  • Martian water resources, atmospheric oxygen production, and regolith investigation.

We also structured the game around realistic mission constraints rather than treating Mars exploration as a simple adventure.

The mechanisms and calculations are areas we continue to test and refine so that the simulations become more consistent and scientifically reliable.

4. Relevance

What it evaluates: How directly the project responds to its selected challenge and how usable and technically feasible the solution is.

How we address it:

MAVEN 2 responds to the selected challenge themes through interconnected gameplay across its three levels:

  • Rover design and operation introduce engineering decisions and exploration.
  • Mission preparation and spacecraft resource management introduce the complexity of long-duration space missions.
  • Mars surface investigations and historical mission references connect previous exploration to future scientific objectives.

The project is also delivered as a browser-based experience, making it accessible without requiring specialized physical hardware.

5. Presentation

What it evaluates: How effectively the team communicates the project, its purpose, and its value.

How we address it:

We built a connected narrative with a clear beginning, progression, and ending.

The Mission Director introduces the mission, the crew members guide the player through different stages, and each level has a distinct objective and identity.

We also use visual interfaces, interactive environments, mission briefings, equipment explanations, historical references, and a final mission report to make the experience easier to understand and follow.

9. NASA Global Awards — Why MAVEN 2 Deserves Recognition

Science

MAVEN 2 turns scientific concepts into interactive mission activities. Players investigate oxygen production, potential water resources, radiation exposure, Martian regolith, controlled plant growing, and rover performance.

They also learn about scientific instruments and their roles before choosing equipment for the mission. Instead of simply reading scientific information, players encounter these topics through decisions and mission objectives.

Art & Technology

MAVEN 2 combines creative visual design with interactive technology.

Its 3D rover workshop allows players to build a rover that directly affects gameplay. The mission interfaces, visual environments, spacecraft views, and interactive elements bring complex space exploration concepts to life.

The project uses technologies such as Three.js, JavaScript, and Canvas to connect the visual experience with actual game interactions. Visual design is not just decoration; it helps players understand and interact with the systems.

Best Use of Storytelling

The three NASA challenge themes are connected through one continuous story rather than presented as separate activities.

The fictional failure of MAVEN 1 creates the motivation for MAVEN 2, while the player progresses from astronaut training and rover engineering to crewed mission planning and Mars exploration.

Recurring characters, mission events, decisions, and Viking 2's guidance make the scientific objectives part of the player's journey instead of disconnected educational information.

The appearance of Viking 1 during landing and the introduction of a personified Viking 2 guide help bring historical Mars exploration into the narrative.

Best Mission Concept

MAVEN 2 presents a connected Mars exploration mission with a logical progression: designing the technology, preparing the crew and payload, surviving the journey, and investigating the Martian environment.

It considers mission constraints such as equipment capabilities, payload, energy, supplies, and environmental risks, connecting individual gameplay activities to a larger exploration objective.

Best Use of Technology

The project uses web technologies to create an interactive browser-based game rather than a static educational presentation.

Players can design and operate a 3D rover, interact with equipment information, use command systems, benefit from assisted navigation, and explore the spacecraft journey from different angles.

Technology is used to make the learning experience interactive and responsive to player decisions.

Galactic Impact

MAVEN 2 aims to inspire interest in space exploration and help students understand the challenges behind future human missions to Mars.

By introducing concepts such as resource efficiency, oxygen and water production, radiation protection, and controlled agriculture, the game connects space exploration with broader questions about sustainability, scientific progress, and humanity's future.

Best Use of Data

MAVEN 2 connects its educational content to NASA mission information and scientific resources.

  • MOXIE: Informs the oxygen-production investigation in Level 3.
  • RAD: Supports the educational content about radiation exposure and protection.
  • Veggie and Advanced Plant Habitat: Inform the controlled plant-growing activities.
  • Perseverance Rover Components: Support the rover engineering concepts in Level 1.
  • ECLSS and Water Recovery: Inform the life-support and water-management concepts in Level 2.

These resources help connect the game's activities to real NASA technologies, experiments, and exploration missions.

10. From the MVP to the Bigger Vision

MAVEN 2 is designed as a complete three-level game experience, while the current MVP establishes the main elements of that experience.

The current project includes:

  • Level 1: Interactive rover design, rover selection, component-dependent commands, different difficulty levels and maps, and assisted Autopilot.
  • Level 2: Mission payload and scientific instrument selection, equipment explanations, automatic equipment transfer, and interactive spacecraft viewing.
  • Level 3: Mars exploration storyline, the Viking 1 landing reference, Viking 2's introduction and guidance, and six mission objectives.

Our Future Plans for MAVEN 2

MAVEN 2 is not just a project we developed for this challenge; it is a project our team has already agreed to continue working on and developing beyond the competition.

We believe it has a much bigger potential than what we have achieved so far. There are still many ideas we want to bring to life, including integrating the full storyline we have written, expanding character interactions and mission events, strengthening the connections between the three levels, and improving the gameplay mechanics and calculations.

We also aim to expand the historical exploration experience by giving players more opportunities to discover the stories, equipment, and scientific contributions of previous Mars missions.

We see MAVEN 2 as an ongoing project with a meaningful concept and plenty of room to grow. Our decision is to keep developing it, building on what we have already created, and turning our current experience into a richer and more complete educational game.

For us, MAVEN 2 is not where the journey ends; it is where a much bigger journey begins.
